name: Oh My Goal News
_comment_group: The news feed of the brand in the folder beside this one, and a
channel in its own right rather than a mode of that one: it is a
separate account cutting separate videos, so the person picking a
channel at the top of the app picks this or Oh My Goal and never both.
It looks exactly like Oh My Goal, and that is the brand rather than a
file nobody finished. The two accounts are one identity - the same
blue card, the same white type, the same face - and a news feed that
announced itself with a different colour would be a second brand for
no reason but that it is a second folder. What separates them is what
is in the video, which is not a thing a pack has any say over.
So it repeats Oh My Goal's answers rather than pointing at them with
`use`. A preset is for a decision several channels SHARE, where a
change to it is meant to reach all of them (see the note at the top of
content/presets/snapchat-caption.json). These two merely agree today.
The day the news feed is given its own colour, a pack that stated its
own is edited in one place; a pack that borrowed its neighbour's would
have to be unpicked from it first.
Read dr-football-us for the face and for why these channels have no
highlight, Hall of Femme for the frame fetch and the card, and Oh My
Goal for these two colours.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report.
A news feed might look like the one channel here with a reason to
keep the words as they were said, and it is worth saying why it does
not. The rewrite does not invent anything - it turns a sentence of
speech into the information that sentence carried, which is what a
caption over a still has to be whether the clip is a goal or an
the audio instead would put half-sentences on the frames.
_comment_title: Set in League Spartan on the brand's electric blue card, in two
colours the user picks per frame - the same answers Oh My Goal gives,
for the reason given at the top of this file.
Everything about how the words are set beyond those is the Snapchat
caption design and is stated once, in

_comment_color: The channel's own answer, and therefore what every frame is set in
until somebody presses a swatch (see state.textColorFor). It is
one of the two in `colors` below, so the white swatch is the one
that shows as chosen on an untouched frame.
Absolute white, and against #312ED5 the exact value matters: an
off-white on a fully saturated blue does not read as a softer
white, it picks up the blue and reads as a caption printed
slightly out of register. Argued at length in oh-my-goal.
_comment_colors: The brand's two colours, offered for the letters and for the card
behind them - the pairing and its inverse.
Why the same list appears twice, and why there are two rows rather
than three, is written out in dr-football-us. The short version of
the second: this channel has no highlight, so a third row would
recolour something that is never drawn, and a row like that is
_comment_highlight: None. Every line of every caption on this channel is set the same
way, and the highlight buttons stand where they stand everywhere
else and go dead with a tooltip saying whose decision that was.
dr-football-us is where this is argued: one cut of League Spartan
means the change of CUT every sibling picks its words out with is
not available, and neither of the two ways round it is worth
having on a caption that is already sitting on a solid card.
_comment_panel: Electric blue, and the fill is the one thing about the card this
pack decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow
are the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.

_comment_branding: No dark gradient. It exists to hold a title legible against the
photograph, and this title is not against the photograph at all - it
is on a card of its own. A scrim over every still would darken forty
pictures to solve a problem the card has already solved.
